newsitem.title: USA: Zitel rises again on year 2000 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Zitel rises again on year 2000 outlook.

text.p: Zitel Corp's stock extended its two-week rise on Friday amid optimism that the company's 35 percent stake in MatriDigm Corp, a software company that specializes in the so-called Year 2000 bug, will pay off big in the next two years, analysts said.
Zitel's revenue from its core business -- making chips for huge disk-drive systems -- also is poised to surge in coming years as demand for storage space rises, analysts said.
By early afternoon Zitel shares were 7-7/8 higher at 60 Nasdaq trading of almost 2.8 million shares, making the stock the third-most active. In the past two weeks, the stock has nearly doubled.
"I have no problem seeing Zitel in two years being a $250 million to $500 million company," said James Schmitt, a money manager at Westcountry Financial in Somis, Calif.
Zitel makes chips that manage the flow of information before it is recorded in giant disk-drive systems used in corporate databases.

In October, Zitel also bought a 35 percent stake in MatriDigm for an undisclosed sum. The closely held software company is working on automating the task of rewriting computer programs that may crash on January 1, 2000.
Much of the world's corporate software was not written to recognize the "00" in dates of the new millennium.
Analysts said MatriDigm has been the engine of Zitel's stock surge in recent weeks.
In the year ended September 30, Zitel had net income of $4.05 million, or $0.52 a share, on revenue of $8.59 million.
